english-language.seca.afterwater.2.a: three cameras; eleven lenses; a notebook already half full of figures (any two)
english-language.seca.afterwater.2.b: Issa, a boy of about ten, offers to carry the camera bag; writer refuses but he insists politely; he carries it holding it carefully and sets it down on driest floor; at end of afternoon writer asks his name, Issa points out his family house, asks whether photos will appear in a paper and whether people will learn Kanta had a good school and football team.
english-language.seca.afterwater.2.c: Realises he only collected pictures of loss and never asked what Kanta was; feels ashamed/humbled; understands Issa wants dignity not pity; sees himself as a guest at a bad time not rescuer; later keeps photo as reminder each figure is a person.
english-language.seca.afterwater.2.d: Plan: Alagiah (anthology text, not supplied) - language of emotion/contrast, first-person witness, structure of shift from detached reporting to personal involvement; AO2 only.
english-language.seca.afterwater.2.e: Plan: compare reporters' initial detachment vs personal connection; Reyes learns from Issa, Alagiah from the people; compare language (similes, figures vs names) and structure; AO3.

english-language.seca.cartrace.1.a: clings to the side of its mountain; drops four hundred metres; twisting back on itself seven times (any two)
english-language.seca.cartrace.1.b: Teams sit on steps drinking coffee and arguing about wheels; man in flowered helmet asleep in cart; grandmother handing out pastries; nobody in charge; cart shaped like bathtub, fish, wardrobe; rules: four wheels, no engine, brakes recommended; Matteo says some skip brakes.
english-language.seca.cartrace.1.c: Race is a tradition over sixty years; hill dominates the rest of the year, race lets townspeople win; community bonding, pride; communal meal; Matteo happy despite bandage.
english-language.seca.cartrace.1.d: Plan: Levine (anthology text, not supplied) - humour, vivid description, hyperbole, structure.
english-language.seca.cartrace.1.e: Plan: compare tone of humour/affection; both outsider observers of eccentric community events; language and structure.

english-language.seca.chess.3.a: sat by the window; chessboard; playing against himself; face as still as a closed door (any two)
english-language.seca.chess.3.b: Learned by watching her grandfather for months pretending to read; learned moves; never asked him to teach her for fear; practised secretly on a drawn board on a cereal box with buttons; entered the tournament without telling anyone; told grandfather she was going to library.
english-language.seca.chess.3.c: Strict, disciplined, ran flat like timetable; ex-railway engineer; silent, gives instructions only; cold but not unkind, fed and paid for school; lonely, plays chess against himself; doesn't know how to relate to her.
english-language.seca.chess.3.d: Plan: Yen Mah (anthology text, not supplied) - contrast of treatment, simple language, structure of listing.
english-language.seca.chess.3.e: Plan: compare relationships with guardians: silence/coldness vs eventual warmth in Mei-hua; contrast with Yen Mah's rejection.

english-language.seca.camels.2.a: strong coffee; engine oil; camel (any two)
english-language.seca.camels.2.b: Long loop of raked sand marked with white posts; no stands; spectators bring chairs, sit on car bonnets or stand in sand with scarves up; several hundred people at 6am; camels in pen near start, tall slim long-legged, brushed coats, blankets and muzzles, looking superior.
english-language.seca.camels.2.c: Khalid loves the camels because of family tradition; cars and robots are new but camels same; watching them he watches his family; race is about heritage not speed/money.
english-language.seca.camels.2.d: Plan: Levine (anthology text, not supplied) - verbs, tension, short sentences.
english-language.seca.camels.2.e: Plan: compare excitement and danger vs tradition; both observers; language/structure.
